title: The Wisdom of Solomon
author: Unknown
description: The Wisdom of Solomon, a book of the Apocrypha (deuterocanonical in Catholic and Orthodox Bibles), here in an early English translation with chapter divisions; the text is affected by OCR errors. Written in Greek in Alexandria probably in the first century BCE by a Hellenistic Jew writing in the persona of King Solomon, it addresses the rulers of the earth. Chapters 1-5 contrast the fate of the righteous and the ungodly and affirm the immortality of the soul. Chapters 6-9 praise personified Wisdom (Sophia), 'a breath of the power of God, and a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty', in language that influenced the Christian Logos doctrine and later Gnostic and Kabbalistic ideas of divine Wisdom. Chapters 10-19 review sacred history, especially the Exodus, as Wisdom's saving work, with a critique of idolatry. It is a key bridge text between Jewish scripture and Greek philosophy.
